manifest.name: Comprehensive Evidence-Based CBT & Schema Knowledge Base

cognitive_distortions.name: All-or-Nothing / Polarized Thinking
cognitive_distortions.description: Viewing situations in absolute, binary terms (e.g., success vs. failure, pure good vs. total disaster) with no recognition of grey areas or middle ground.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Prefrontal cognitive inflexibility amplifying amygdalar threat response when an outcome deviates even slightly from an idealized standard.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: If this presentation isn't 100% flawless, my entire career is ruined.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: What exists on the continuum between 0% and 100%? Can something be imperfect AND still deeply worthwhile?
socratic_questions: Are you evaluating this on a 0-to-100 scale, or treating anything under 100 as 0?
How would you view this outcome if a respected mentor achieved the same result?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Notice if your body is holding rigid tension or held breath as if braced for catastrophe.

cognitive_distortions.name: Overgeneralization
cognitive_distortions.description: Taking a single negative incident and concluding that it defines a permanent, inescapable universal rule for the future.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Faulty predictive coding where one negative data point triggers an overweighted global prior probability.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: I stumbled during my interview; I will never find a good job anywhere.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: Is one isolated event mathematically sufficient to predict all future attempts across time?
socratic_questions: What evidence exists that this specific outcome will inevitably repeat every single time?
Have you ever experienced a setback that later led to an unexpected positive resolution?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Release the constriction in your chest; separate this one moment from your future timeline.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(never again|every single time|always happens to me|everyone rejects me|i will always fail)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Mental Filter (Selective Abstraction)
cognitive_distortions.description: Dwelling exclusively on a single negative detail while filtering out and blinding oneself to numerous positive or neutral elements.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Hyperactive salience network prioritizing negative threat cues while habituating to safety signals.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: Out of twenty positive reviews, one client left 3 stars—I am incompetent.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: If you zoom out to look at the entire landscape rather than this one pixel, what is the full picture?
socratic_questions: What positive or neutral facts are being obscured by focusing entirely on this one point?
If you created a pie chart of the total feedback, what percentage does this negative detail actually occupy?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Widen your peripheral field of view physically to help your cognitive lens widen as well.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(only focus on|all that matters is the bad|ignored the good|forgot all the compliments)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Disqualifying the Positive
cognitive_distortions.description: Actively rejecting positive experiences, compliments, or accomplishments by insisting they 'don't count' or were purely accidental.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Schema preservation bias: cognitive dissonance reduction defending a core belief of defectiveness against contradictory evidence.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: They only praised my work because they felt sorry for me or were being polite.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: What would happen if you accepted this genuine data point as real evidence of your competence?
socratic_questions: Why is negative feedback treated as absolute truth, but positive feedback dismissed as luck or pity?
What specific effort, skill, or preparation did you invest that contributed to this success?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Place a hand over your heart and allow yourself to absorb the warmth of your real effort.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(just luck|they were just being nice|doesn't count|anyone could have done that|fluke)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Jumping to Conclusions: Mind Reading
cognitive_distortions.description: Assuming you know with absolute certainty what others are thinking, feeling, or intending, almost always assuming a negative judgment.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Dysfunctional social-cognition heuristics projecting internal shame or anxiety onto ambiguous social cues.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: She looked at her watch while I was talking; she clearly thinks I'm boring and stupid.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: What are three alternative explanations for their behavior that have nothing to do with judging you?
socratic_questions: Did they explicitly tell you that, or is your mind filling in an unverified script?
Could they be tired, preoccupied, hungry, or managing their own internal stressors?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Unclench your jaw and gently remind yourself: 'I do not have to carry other people's internal worlds.'
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(they think i'm|she hates me|he thinks i'm stupid|everyone in the room was judging me|i know what they're thinking)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Jumping to Conclusions: Fortune Telling
cognitive_distortions.description: Anticipating that future events will turn out disastrously and treating this prediction as an established, inevitable fact.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Hyper-anticipatory anxiety stimulating adrenaline surges for imagined futures that have not yet occurred.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: I know I'm going to have a panic attack and embarrass myself during tomorrow's meeting.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: Has your crystal ball ever been wrong in the past? What is the most realistic outcome?
socratic_questions: What are the odds of the worst-case scenario happening vs. a moderate, manageable outcome?
If the worst case did happen, what concrete coping tools and strengths would you deploy?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Take a slow 4-second exhale. Bring your awareness into this exact present second—where you are safe.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(i know it will fail|i'm going to mess up|it's bound to go wrong|nothing will ever work out)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Magnification (Catastrophizing)
cognitive_distortions.description: Exaggerating the importance, likelihood, or unbearable severity of an unwanted event, framing it as an insurmountable nightmare.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Underestimation of coping capacity coupled with overestimation of threat probability.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: If I fail this exam, my life is completely over and I will end up homeless.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: Is this a true life-threatening emergency, or is it an intensely uncomfortable and frustrating problem?
socratic_questions: On a scale from 1 (minor annoyance) to 100 (plane crash), where does this event realistically sit?
How will this matter 1 year from now? What is your resilient plan to navigate it?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Double nasal inhale, long open-mouth sigh (Physiological Sigh) to break the adrenaline spike.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(worst thing ever|life is over|end of the world|can't survive this|unbearable disaster)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Minimization
cognitive_distortions.description: Inappropriately shrinking one's own positive qualities, resources, or coping abilities until they seem insignificant.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Deficit-focused cognitive filtering suppressing self-efficacy signals.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: Yes, I managed that crisis, but that was just basic common sense—anyone could have done it.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: If you gave yourself honest credit for your resilience, what would you acknowledge?
socratic_questions: What specific strengths and endurance did you exhibit during this challenge?
Why is it difficult to let yourself feel genuine self-respect for what you overcame?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Lengthen your spine and feel the solid ground beneath your feet supporting your strength.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(no big deal|not impressive|bare minimum|i just got lucky|not really an achievement)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Emotional Reasoning
cognitive_distortions.description: Assuming that because you feel a certain intense emotion, that emotion must reflect the objective, factual state of reality.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Interoceptive confusion treating limbic emotional arousal as external sensory evidence.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: I feel terrified and anxious right now, so something terrible must be about to happen.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: Feelings are real neurochemical events, but are they always factual reflections of the outside world?
socratic_questions: Can you feel intense guilt without having actually committed a wrongdoing?
Can you feel deep fear while being physically completely safe in your current environment?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Place both feet flat on the floor. Name 3 physical objects around you to re-anchor in sensory reality.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(i feel like a failure so i must be|i feel guilty so i'm bad|i feel scared so it's dangerous)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: 'Should' and 'Must' Statements
cognitive_distortions.description: Operating from rigid, moralistic rules about how oneself, others, or the universe 'should', 'must', or 'ought' to behave.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Internalized hyper-demanding parent schemas producing perpetual chronic guilt, shame, or frustration.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: I should always be productive. I shouldn't be feeling tired on a Saturday afternoon.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: What happens if you replace 'I should' with 'I would prefer to' or 'It would be nice if'?
socratic_questions: Where did this unwritten absolute rule come from? Is it serving your health or depleting you?
Are you holding human biological limitations to an impossible superhuman standard?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Drop your shoulders away from your ears. Grant your body permission to be human today.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(i should have|i shouldn't feel|i must always|they ought to|i have to be perfect)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Labeling and Global Mislabeling
cognitive_distortions.description: Assigning a harsh, definitive global label to oneself or others based on a single behavior or mistake rather than describing the action accurately.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Essentialist cognitive attribution collapsing behavioral complexity into a fixed negative trait.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: I made an error on the budget sheet; I am an absolute idiot and a fraud.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: You made a specific human error. Does making a mistake make your entire being an error?
socratic_questions: Is there a distinction between 'I made a mistake' and 'I am a failure'?
How would you describe your action with objective, compassionate behavioral language?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Place your hands on your lap palm-up in an open, receptive posture of self-forgiveness.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(i am a loser|i am an idiot|i'm such a failure|i'm broken|i'm toxic|i'm useless)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Personalization & Excessive Responsibility
cognitive_distortions.description: Holding oneself directly and solely responsible for negative events that are largely or entirely beyond one's personal control.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Egocentric causal attribution error driven by excessive hyper-responsibility schemas.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: My parents are arguing again—if only I were a better child, they would be happy.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: What other external factors, choices, and life pressures contributed to this outcome?
socratic_questions: Are you taking 100% of the blame for a situation involving multiple autonomous adults?
If you drew a pie chart of all factors involved, how much belongs to others and circumstances?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Exhale deeply and visualize putting down a heavy backpack that does not belong to you.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(it's all my fault|i ruined everything for them|if only i had done better they wouldn't suffer)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Blaming (Externalization)
cognitive_distortions.description: Holding other people or external circumstances entirely responsible for one's own emotional state, disowning personal agency.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Victimhood schema shielding the self from vulnerability by projecting all locus of control outward.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: My partner makes me feel miserable every single day; I can't be happy until they change.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: While others' actions hurt, what is one boundary or response you have 100% power to choose today?
socratic_questions: Where does their responsibility end and your personal sovereignty begin?
What small boundary would protect your peace regardless of how they behave?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Feel your core engage. Ground into your own personal boundaries and emotional sovereignty.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(they ruined my life|he made me do it|i can't be happy because of them|they are destroying my peace)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Fallacy of Control (External vs. Internal)
cognitive_distortions.description: Either believing you have total control over everything and everyone (omnipotence), or believing you have zero control over your own choices (helplessness).
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Split locus of control oscillating between overwhelming hyper-responsibility and catastrophic surrender.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: I have to fix everyone's problems or disaster will strike / There's nothing I can do, I'm completely helpless.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: What lies strictly within your direct circle of control vs. outside of it?
socratic_questions: Can you control another person's feelings, or only your own words and boundaries?
What is one concrete, actionable choice you DO have in this exact moment?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Place one hand on your chest and one on your belly. Direct your attention to your own breath.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(i have to fix everything|i have no choice at all|i am completely powerless|i'm responsible for their feelings)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Fallacy of Fairness
cognitive_distortions.description: Believing that life, systems, or relationships must always conform to an absolute standard of fairness, producing chronic resentment.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Inability to tolerate life's inherent existential randomness and interpersonal imbalances.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: It isn't fair that they got promoted after I worked harder—life is fundamentally rigged against me.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: Life is often asymmetrical, but does dwelling in bitterness help you move toward what you value?
socratic_questions: Is fairness a natural law of the physical universe, or a human ethical construct?
How can you channel this frustration into values-aligned action rather than toxic resentment?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Acknowledge the stinging pain of unfairness with compassion, then release the clenched fist.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(it's not fair|why do bad things only happen to me|they don't deserve it|life is unfair)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Fallacy of Change
cognitive_distortions.description: Expecting that other people will and must change to suit our needs if we just pressure, plead, or accommodate them enough.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Subjugation or enmeshment schema attaching one's own emotional well-being to another person's transformation.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: If I just explain it to him one more time with enough passion, he will finally understand and change.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: If this person never changes a single habit, what decision honors your long-term health?
socratic_questions: How many times have you had this exact conversation without lasting change?
Are you accepting who they actually are today, or relating to a fantasy version of who they could be?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Breathe into your spine. Stand firmly in your own reality rather than trying to sculpt another's.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(if only they would change|i can fix them|they will change for me|if i explain one more time)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Always Being Right
cognitive_distortions.description: Continually putting others on trial to prove that one's own opinions, actions, and perspectives are the only correct ones.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Vulnerability avoidance shielding an underlying core schema of defectiveness or fear of shame.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: I don't care if it causes a huge fight—I have to prove that my method was the correct one.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: Would you rather be rigidly 'right', or connected, peaceful, and emotionally safe?
socratic_questions: What underlying fear or vulnerability arises if you acknowledge another valid perspective?
What is the relational cost of needing to win every disagreement?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Softly soften your belly and throat. Notice the safety in not needing to defend yourself right now.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(i have to prove i was right|i know i'm right|they are completely wrong|i can't let them win the argument)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Heaven's Reward Fallacy
cognitive_distortions.description: Sacrificing oneself and denying personal needs with the implicit expectation of a magical, cosmic reward or unconditional appreciation.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Self-sacrifice schema masking suppressed needs under a veneer of altruism, generating hidden rage.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: I sacrificed my entire weekend helping everyone else, and nobody even thanked me or noticed.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: Did you choose this sacrifice from genuine freely-given joy, or from a covert contract expecting reward?
socratic_questions: Was the contract explicitly agreed upon by both parties, or assumed silently in your mind?
How can you express your real needs and boundaries directly instead of through self-sacrifice?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Inhale deeply into your belly. Reclaim your right to take care of your own needs first.
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(after all i did for them|nobody appreciates my sacrifice|i gave up everything for this|i suffer in silence)\b

cognitive_distortions.name: Double Standard Thinking
cognitive_distortions.description: Applying brutal, unforgiving standards to oneself while extending gentle, unconditional compassion and understanding to others.
cognitive_distortions.clinical_mechanism: Hyperactive punitive parent internal voice contrasting with well-developed external empathy.
cognitive_distortions.example_thought: If my friend made this mistake I would comfort them, but because it's me, I am disgusting.
cognitive_distortions.reframing_prompt: What would it feel like to treat yourself with the exact same kindness you offer your best friend?
socratic_questions: Why do you hold yourself to a cruel code of punishment that you would never inflict on someone you love?
What would happen if you spoke to yourself with the warmth of a loving guardian right now?
cognitive_distortions.somatic_anchor: Cross your arms gently over your chest in a self-compassion hug (Butterfly Touch).
cognitive_distortions.trigger_regex: \b(if it were anyone else it's fine but for me|i'm harder on myself|i don't deserve the same kindness)\b

maladaptive_schemas.name: Abandonment / Instability
maladaptive_schemas.core_belief: Anyone close to me will inevitably leave, die, or find someone better, leaving me forever alone.
maladaptive_schemas.behavioral_pattern: Hypervigilance to partner withdrawal, clinginess, or preemptively pushing people away.
maladaptive_schemas.somatic_marker: Hollow vacuum in the upper chest, throat tightness, visceral drop in stomach.

maladaptive_schemas.name: Mistrust / Abuse
maladaptive_schemas.core_belief: People will hurt, deceive, exploit, or take advantage of me if I let my guard down.
maladaptive_schemas.behavioral_pattern: Guardedness, testing relationships, paranoia in close intimacy.
maladaptive_schemas.somatic_marker: Chronic hyper-tension in jaw, back of neck, and shoulder blades.

maladaptive_schemas.name: Emotional Deprivation
maladaptive_schemas.core_belief: My primary emotional needs for nurturance, empathy, and protection will never be met by others.
maladaptive_schemas.behavioral_pattern: Not asking for help, acting emotionally self-contained while feeling profoundly lonely.
maladaptive_schemas.somatic_marker: Deep emotional chill, heavy chest pressure, flat breathing.

maladaptive_schemas.name: Defectiveness / Shame
maladaptive_schemas.core_belief: I am inwardly flawed, bad, unlovable, or inferior; if anyone sees the real me, they will be repulsed.
maladaptive_schemas.behavioral_pattern: Hiding mistakes, excessive shame, hypersensitivity to criticism, perfectionist masking.
maladaptive_schemas.somatic_marker: Flushing in the face and neck, curling posture, sinking feeling in the solar plexus.

maladaptive_schemas.name: Failure
maladaptive_schemas.core_belief: I am inherently inadequate and will inevitably fail in comparison to my peers in work and life.
maladaptive_schemas.somatic_marker: Lethargy in limbs, chronic slump, avoidance of eye contact.

maladaptive_schemas.name: Unrelenting Standards / Hypercriticalness
maladaptive_schemas.core_belief: I must constantly strive to meet exceptionally high internalized standards to avoid severe shame or failure.
maladaptive_schemas.behavioral_pattern: Workaholism, perfectionism, inability to rest without guilt, rigid rule enforcement.
maladaptive_schemas.somatic_marker: Constricted shallow breathing, chronic muscle tension, elevated resting heart rate.

clinical_protocols.name: 7-Column Dysfunctional Thought Record (DTR)
clinical_protocols.evidence_base: Beck Cognitive Therapy Rating Scale (CTRS) Gold Standard
steps: 1. Situation (Who, What, Where, When)
2. Emotion / Mood (Name emotion and rate intensity 0-100%)
3. Automatic Thought (Identify the exact hot cognitions)
4. Evidence Supporting the Thought (Factual, objective data only)
5. Evidence Against the Thought (Objective contrary data)
6. Balanced Alternative Thought (Reframed realistic perspective)
7. Re-rate Outcome Emotion (Re-measure emotional intensity 0-100%)

clinical_protocols.name: Downward Arrow Technique
clinical_protocols.evidence_base: Core Schema & Intermediate Belief Elicitation Protocol
steps: 1. Start with the surface automatic thought (e.g., 'I made a mistake at work')
2. Ask: 'If that were true, what would that mean to you?'
3. Unpack the next layer (e.g., 'My manager will think I am incompetent')
4. Ask: 'And if your manager thought that, what does that mean about you?'
5. Reach the core schema (e.g., 'It means I am inherently defective and unlovable')
6. Apply cognitive restructuring directly at the root schema level

clinical_protocols.name: Decatastrophizing Matrix (What If? Protocol)
steps: 1. Worst-Case Scenario: What is the absolute worst that could realistically happen?
2. Best-Case Scenario: What is the most optimistic, ideal outcome possible?
3. Most-Likely Scenario: What is the statistically probable, realistic outcome?
4. Concrete Coping Action Plan: If the worst case occurred, what exact step 1, 2, and 3 would you take?

clinical_protocols.name: 3rd-Wave ACT Cognitive Defusion Toolkit
steps: 1. Prefix Framing: Replace 'I am a failure' with 'I am noticing the thought that I am a failure'
2. Naming the Story: 'Ah, here is my familiar Impostor Story playing again'
3. Leaves on a Stream: Visualize each thought written on a leaf floating smoothly downstream
4. Physicalizing Metaphor: If this thought had a shape, color, and weight, what would it look like?
